notes: an audit pass. A per-tool policy you set by hand now beats the chat mode both ways: 'always ask' used to be skipped in Allow all and in Plan mode, so a tool you had pinned to ask ran silently — only 'deny' was ever honoured, while the Permissions panel promised otherwise. fs_move no longer destroys the file when source and destination are the same path, or differ only in capitalisation — which is what a rename like a.txt to A.txt looks like to macOS and Windows, where both names are one file, and where the model was being told to pass overwrite: true to get past it. A browser profile that refuses local storage no longer leaves a window that looks finished and does nothing: the failure is reported in a red bar, the rest of the app still starts, and the database says so on every kind of failure rather than only when another tab holds an older version. An empty answer from the proxy's /model/info stops wiping every context window and price the app had. A Python run that times out or is stopped tells the other runs it restarted what actually happened to them instead of handing them its own error, and a blank Pyodide URL is a message rather than a crash. Importing a skill file is validated like the other two ways of making one, so an imported copy.md can no longer become a skill that /copy could never reach. Reverting a file no longer stops recording what a chat running in the background writes. Plus the smaller things: a run and the message that started it can no longer end up in two different chats, a Retry-After of five minutes no longer pins a toast for five minutes, the file index is invalidated after a write lands rather than before, git_status says why a file could not be read, and unreadable usage counters start at zero instead of ending the turn
